Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
On June 12th at Fingal County Council’s AGM, Cllr Tony 
Murphy was elected Mayor of Fingal and Cllr Luke Corkery 
was elected Deputy Mayor. First elected as an Independent 
candidate in 2014, Cllr Murphy has stated, as Mayor he will 
seek to foster growth within the local economy, improve 
infrastructure and support initiatives to see people housed 
within thriving and vibrant communities. Joining him for 
the term is Deputy Mayor Luke Corkery, who was first 
elected as a Fine Gael Councillor in the 2024 local election 
representing his hometown of Swords. Also at the AGM, 
Councillors elected the new Chairs of the three local area 
committees. These committees focus on the local delivery 
of services within their respective regions, addressing 
issues such as roads, litter, housing, playgrounds, and 
libraries. The newly elected Chairs for this year are: 
Balbriggan/Rush-Lusk/Swords: 
Cllr. 
Tom 
O'Leary; 
Blanchardstown-Mulhuddart/ 
Castleknock/Ongar: 
Cllr. 
Eimear 
Carbone-Mangan and 
Howth-Malahide: 
Cllr. 
Aoibhinn Tormey. I wish all the newly appointed cllrs the 
very best in their roles and I look forward to working with 
them and the other elected members throughout the year.   
Recent spells of sunshine have seen thousands of visitors 
to our beaches, harbours and public amenities to enjoy the 
fine weather. As the bathing season continues, more and 
more people will take to the beaches to swim, enjoy water 
sports and boating activities. I am very pleased that Fingal 
County Council has been awarded two Blue Flags and a 
Green Coast Award for 2026. These awards are highly 
prestigious and are the benchmark for environmental 
excellence. Velvet Strand in Portmarnock and Balcarrick 
Beach in Donabate have once again secured Blue Flag 
status, while Balcarrick Beach has also retained its Green 
Coast Award. Fingal County Council consistently works to 
maintain excellent standards in terms of safety, water 
quality and environmental management along our 
coastline. 
Collaboration 
with 
local 
communities 
is 
important in maintaining standards and co-operation from 
visitors to the beaches is vital in terms of leaving nothing 
behind after their visit. I would like to pay tribute to 
everyone involved with the cleaning and maintenance of 
our beautiful beaches – we are fortunate to have 88km of 
coastline in Fingal and it is a testament to all that we are 
recognised year after year with our Blue Flag and Green 
Coast Awards. 
The first phase of consultation for the Dunsink Urban Area 
Plan was launched last month. The draft Urban Area Plan 
for “Dunsink City Quarter” visualises a plan to convert lands 
at Dunsink into a brand new residential-led mixed-use 
community. Whilst sensitively observing cultural and 
heritage 
sites 
of 
importance 
including 
Dunsink 
Observatory, the Royal Canal and the Tolka Valley, the new  
 
neighbourhood will deliver new homes alongside essential 
community facilities, employment opportunities, and 
educational provision. The lands at Dunsink, totalling 435 
hectares, represent one of the most significant remaining 
landbanks within Dublin. Close to established residential 
neighbourhoods including Finglas, Ashtown, Castleknock 
and Blanchardstown, the development is adjacent to two 
mainline railway stations and will see extended bus routes 
and the extension of the LUAS Green Line to Tyrellstown 
which will offer commuters greater flexibility and frequent, 
efficient services. An estimated 18,500 mixed tenure 
homes will be delivered in the proposed plan alongside a 
Cultural Quarter centred on Dunsink Observatory as well 
as a new Regional Park and Recreational Hub on the former 
landfill site. The new development will also benefit from 
community infrastructure including community centres, 
creches, and schools. This incredibly ambitious blueprint 
for living represents Fingal County Council’s unwavering 
commitment to building sustainable, accessible and 
inclusive communities. We have secured funding in excess 
of €20 million under the Government’s new €1 billion 
Housing Infrastructure Investment Fund (HIIF) to deliver 
key 
upgrades 
at 
the 
Dunsink 
Lands, 
including 
improvements to Scribblestown Lane and Dunsinea Lane 
and associated infrastructure. The investment will support 
road widening and realignment, alongside the delivery of a 
new active travel greenway, enabling the development of 
this strategically important landbank. The consultation 
period will remain open until close of business on Friday, 
31st July and you can find all the details on our website and 
social media channels. I look forward to bringing you 
updates on the progress of the Dunsink City Quarter in due 
course. 
As we reflect on a truly fantastic series of concerts at 
Malahide Castle, I would like to offer my congratulations to 
everyone involved with the process. As you would expect, 
a phenomenal amount of work is required from the very 
start of planning these events several months in advance 
until the last concert goer leaves the venue. We are 
fortunate to have highly experienced people within the 
organisation whose event management, organisational 
and procedural expertise are invaluable to the success of 
the events. In the planning process, we liaise closely with a 
key group of stakeholders to ensure the safety and 
wellbeing of the public whilst ensuring all possible logistics 
are covered. I am very pleased to have had such positive 
feedback on this year’s concerts and if you attended some 
of them, I hope you had a really enjoyable evening. 
Best wishes, 
AnnMarie Farrelly - Chief Executive

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
Explore Fingal Familiarisation Visit 
 
The tourism product in Fingal continues to develop 
and expand. 
 
Page 4 
This year several new tours are on offer and the 
Fingal tourism team with a representative from Fáilte 
Ireland participated in an industry familiarisation visit 
on Thursday 11th June to experience three of them. 
At each venue, as well as doing the tours, key 
personnel provided briefings to the visitors.  
The first stop was Ardgillan Castle and Demesne 
which has recently launched an immersive, self-
guided audio tour designed especially for families. 
This was followed by a visit to McNally Family Farm, a 
fourth-generation farm in north Fingal renowned for 
its organic fruit and vegetable production, café and 
popular farm shop. Their farm tour, introduced last 
year, has been improved to include a food offering in 
a new event space. The final visit was to Celtic Tweed 
in Balbriggan for their tour, an award-winning Irish 
fashion and design business combining traditional 
craftsmanship with contemporary Irish design. 
The day provided an opportunity to learn more about 
the visitor experiences available across Fingal and to 
strengthen 
connections 
between 
tourism 
stakeholders and industry partners. 
 
 
 
First Explore Fingal market in Blanchardstown 
The 
inaugural 
Explore 
Fingal 
Markets 
Blanchardstown was held at Millennium Park in June. 
The event featured a hot food (food truck) market 
alongside live musical entertainment and was 
designed to bring together a variety of cuisines in a 
welcoming open space. The market attracted strong 
footfall for its first outing and provided an 
opportunity to showcase local businesses while 
creating a vibrant community atmosphere.

This pilot initiative forms part of the wider Explore 
Fingal Markets programme, which aims to support 
local enterprise and enhance the visitor experience 
across the county.  
 
Explore Fingal – a new presence at Flavours of 
Fingal  
Fingal’s new destination tourism brand Explore 
Fingal will play a prominent role at Flavours of Fingal 
this year. A dedicated area in the walled garden will 
showcase both the new brand and some of the 
outstanding attractions Fingal has to offer. Everyone 
is invited to drop in, meet the tourism team and find 
out more about the county’s tourism offering. Golf 
will be highlighted as a USP and some of the county’s 
24 golf clubs will be on hand to talk with visitors.  New 
eye-catching signage around the showgrounds will 
reinforce the role of the Explore Fingal brand.

Malahide Castle will host a live performance of

Newbridge House and Farm 
Newbridge House is to receive upgraded internet 
with the arrival of a fibre connection from National 
Broadband Ireland. A proposal for installation of the 
new connection which respects the historic structure 
has been in the works with IT for several months and 
will improve connectivity on the site, for staff and 
visitors alike. 
 
The Casino Model Railway Museum 
 
 
 
The Casino had a recent facelift as part of 
preparations for the Explore Fingal food market, with 
a fresh coat of paint, new flooring in the toilets and 
the arrival of Hibernia. Hibernia is a mobile catering 
unit situated on the grounds. Wrapped to look like a 
railway carriage, the cafe offers hot food and drinks 
and is open every Saturday as part of the market. 
 
Skerries Mills 
 
 
 
The new Outdoor Biodiversity Classroom at Skerries 
Mills has welcomed its first school group to learn 
about nature and the importance of biodiversity.   
 
The project was a collaboration between the Skerries 
Mills Men's Shed Group and Skerries Mills and the

project was funded by the Men's Shed under their 
National Lottery allocation. It is planned that the 
garden will be an addition to the School Tour and 
local experts are on hand to deliver workshops as 
requested.

Creative Places Balbriggan

Creative Places Balbriggan celebrated Cruinniú na 
nÓg by hosting 3 days of introductory workshops to 
architecture and construction in the first week of 
June. “Building Composition” was facilitated by award 
winning Balbriggan Architects Islander and attended 
by 12-14 year olds from all of the secondary schools 
in Balbriggan. Their 3 days of work were showcase at 
“Creative Compositions”, which was a special 
exhibition at The Lark Concert Hall on Cruinniú na 
nÓg, attended by the Mayor of Fingal and County Arts 
Officer as well as the participants and their families. 
The Creative Places Coordinator also presented to 
the new Creative Coastal Communities Network 
across UK and Ireland. The talk addressed the 3 work 
pillars of the CPB strategy with a particular focus on 
Creative Youth research and engagement and 
various Arts Office youth supports available in the 
county such as the Youth and Education section of 
the Arts Office,  Foróige and Comhairle na nÓg.

Discovering Drumanagh

Discovering Drumanagh a collaborative project 
supported by Creative Fingal with Fingal Heritage 
Office and Fingal Libraries culminated in the launch 
of a publication of the same name in Rush Library 
on 17th June. 
 
• 
The project is the creative response by 
4th Class in St. Catherine’s NS, Rush to 
archaeological findings at Drumanagh Fort 
near Rush. 
• 
Fingal-based author and illustrator, Niamh 
Sharkey took up residency in the school over 
several weeks. After a visit to the site, Niamh 
worked with the children to bring their 
interpretation of Drumanagh and its history 
to life, and arranged their work into a 
publication, Discovery Drumanagh. 
• 
Every child in the school will be gifted a copy 
of the booklet which will also be available in 
Fingal libraries and on Borrowbox as a 
downloadable Ebook.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and 
Tenant In-situ Acquisitions  
Fingal County Council is aware that households in the 
Fingal area who may have received a notice to quit, 
which is also referred to as a notice of termination, 
from their landlord may be worried or unsure of 
what to do.  
 
Fingal County Council and the Dublin Regional 
Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to advise 
anyone affected of the services that are available to 
them in these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County Council 
as soon as they receive a notice from their 
landlord. The contact details for Fingal County 
Council are provided at the bottom of this page.  
 
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff 
in the Housing Department will take note of the 
termination date. The Council advises the tenant to 
refer the notice to Threshold, a service funded by the 
DRHE to provide a Tenancy Protection Service for 
private renters in the Dublin Region, including Fingal.  
 
Page 79 
Threshold can also be contacted directly on 
Freephone 1800 454 454 or via their website 
www.threshold.ie which contains more information 
and advice on the validity of your notice.  The 
Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice 
on applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising 
the person on the level of Housing Assistance 
Payment (HAP) they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a 
last resort if no other alternative can be identified.   
 Fingal County Council continues to liaise with other 
Dublin and neighboring local authorities to deal with 
tenancy issues that may require an inter-authority 
approach.  In particular, we are working closely with 
our colleagues in the other Dublin Local Authorities 
on the implementation of the Government policy and 
guidance, with a focus on the needs of tenants.   
  
Whilst the Council will, in the context of current 
circumstances, adopt flexibility in dealing with 
potential acquisitions of properties with tenants in 
situ, any acquisition is subject to appropriate due 
diligence and checks before any commitment is 
made to acquire, including, for example, determining 
that a valid notice of termination is in place, the 
tenant has a social housing need, and the condition 
and valuation of the property.  
  
The Government has put forward options to allow 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing to 
remain in their homes, including schemes to support 
the purchase of homes and a Cost Rental in-situ 
Scheme. The Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ Scheme is 
available for tenants who are not eligible for social 
housing and are at risk of homelessness. The DHLGH 
has advised that local authorities are to be the first 
point of contact for this scheme, but it is managed by 
the Housing Agency. Under the scheme, the Housing 
Agency can purchase a property and rent it to the 
tenant. Fingal County Council will undertake an initial 
assessment of the tenant’s circumstances and refer 
details to the Housing Agency for consideration, 
where the tenant is at risk of homelessness and the 
Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ scheme applies.

The Housing Agency will then contact the landlord 
about the purchase of the property.  
  
Where a tenant wishes to purchase their home from 
the landlord, local authorities can provide advice 
about the Local Authority Home Loan scheme. The 
Government is examining implementing a ‘right of 
first refusal’ for tenants to purchase their homes, as 
well as expanding the First Home shared equity

information on these when available.   Works around
